[build-order:internal].reason: An unreachable internal invariant guard: the Build_Sequence only ever produces nodes derived from the discovered set, so no committed tree can make it emit a node absent from that set; it exists to turn a future refactor's broken invariant into a named error instead of a silent crash.

[build-order:divergence].reason: A self-consistency assertion: the Workspace_Build_Order and the Tsc_Root_Order both derive from the single buildSequence primitive with identical statement assignment and identical within-statement sort, so any shared pair is ordered identically and divergence can arise only from a future Build_System bug, not from any input.

[config:unreadable].reason: A config file that exists but cannot be read; git records no mode beyond the execute bit and a CI umask is not ours to choose, so committed bytes cannot express the unreadable state.

[config:root-unreadable].reason: A Discovery_Root that exists but cannot be read; same permission-state reason as [config:unreadable].

[dev:compile].reason: A runtime status line, not a fault: the Dev_Supervisor prints it every watch cycle ("cycle complete: N error(s)"); it matches the Diagnostic_Tag shape but is normal progress output no Project_Directory input provokes as an error.

[image-tree:framework-output].reason: A self-consistency assertion over the assembler's own output: a Framework_Singleton is always a tsc root, so a successful tsc pass always emits its dist; the only way its dist is absent is a stale gitignored .tsbuildinfo, a runtime state committed bytes cannot express.

[image-tree:missing].reason: A self-consistency assertion: the assembler copies exactly plan.stage into a freshly emptied outDir and then re-reads it, so a justified entry can be missing only through an assembler bug, never through a committed input.

[image-tree:unjustified].reason: A self-consistency assertion: the assembler copies only plan.stage entries into a freshly emptied outDir outside the checked-out tree, so a committed fixture cannot inject an extra scoped entry; only an assembler bug could.

[scope:literal].reason: A self-consistency assertion over the Build_System's own source: the check scans the fixed literal packages/build-tools/src, never the Project_Directory, so a scope literal it flags is a Build_System authoring mistake, never a committed fixture input.
